source_grounding.call_chain_traced: actix handler get_collection_aliases (src/actix/api/collections_api.rs:95, route #[get("/collections/{collection_name}/aliases")], plain CollectionPath — no strict validation) -> do_list_collection_aliases (src/common/collections.rs:167) -> toc.collection_aliases (toc/mod.rs:434) -> AliasPersistence::collection_aliases (alias_mapping.rs:114): a pure scan of the alias_name->collection_name map returning all aliases whose target equals the given string. Nowhere in this chain is collection existence checked: the alias map is keyed by alias, the codebase's existence machinery (Checker::validate_collection_exists, collections_ops.rs:25, StorageError::not_found 'Collection `X` doesn't exist!') and resolve_name() (toc/mod.rs:410, used by toc.get_collection) are NOT invoked; the function is infallible with respect to collection existence and always returns Ok(200). Contrast: do_get_collection/do_collection_exists/do_list_snapshots/do_get_collection_shard_keys/do_get_collection_cluster all call toc.get_collection().await? first and therefore 404 on unknown names. The write path (update_aliases create_alias) validates existence, and delete_collection removes the name's aliases (remove_collection), so after a drop the read-side scan yields empty rather than erroring. OpenAPI generation (openapi/openapi-collections.ytt.yaml:399-413) documents this GET with responses = {200 CollectionsAliasesResponse} plus the generic 4XX/default error macros — no op-specific 404. verification_outcome determination: the source contains NO validation implementing the assertion's 'unknown collection -> HTTP 404' promise on this code path (nothing can raise NotFound here), and no by-design declaration exists (no comment/docstring/maintainer citation marks the 200-empty-for-missing-collection behavior as intentional — the same file family validates existence on the write path and on every sibling read path, so the omission is an inconsistency, not a declared design).

mundane_explanation.surviving: GET /collections/{collection_name}/aliases performs no collection-existence validation on its read path (do_list_collection_aliases -> toc.collection_aliases -> pure alias-map scan; unlike describe/count/snapshots faces which all toc.get_collection().await? -> 404), so a never-created or already-deleted collection name returns HTTP 200 {'result':{'aliases':[]},'status':'ok'} — indistinguishable from an alias-free existing collection and contradicting the contract assertion's 404 limb. Reproduced on 3 independent scripts (semantic_aliases_collection_list_002, boundary_aliases_collection_list_004, state_aliases_collection_list_001) with distinct unique names against the same v1.18.0 instance; positive controls on the same endpoint (semantic_aliases_collection_list_001/004) returned proper 200 alias payloads, and the never-created name was API-confirmed non-existent (guard DELETE result:false; describe 404).
